structural: The text prescribes these structural obligations, and the supplied roots meet each one.

- **Type and path.** The text requires `trust_but_verify::graph::NodePath` to be `pub struct NodePath { /* private fields */ }`. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph.rs#struct[NodePath]` declares it `pub` in the `graph` module. Its only field, `segments: Vec<String>`, is private, and the doc comment includes a `compile_fail` doctest that checks this. A struct with public fields would still produce the same runtime results, so this clause is a real structural obligation. The root meets it.
- **Constructor signature.** The text requires `pub fn new(segments: Vec<String>) -> Self`. `impl[NodePath]/fn[new]` has exactly that signature and stores the vector unchanged.
- **Accessor signature.** The text requires `pub fn segments(&self) -> &[String]`. `impl[NodePath]/fn[segments]` has exactly that signature and returns `&self.segments`, a borrowed slice.
- **Trait implementations.** The text requires `Clone`, `Debug`, `Deserialize`, `Hash`, `PartialEq`, `Serialize` and `Eq`. The `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]` on `struct[NodePath]` covers all seven.

The three roots carry `{impl}`, and the struct also carries `{test}`. All three obligations are implemented directly in the roots, with no delegation to follow.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.node_path_struct` has these testable obligations. All of them have test evidence.

- **Constructor and accessor.** `NodePath::new(Vec<String>)` must preserve the segments, and `segments()` must return them in order as `&[String]`.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[node_paths_round_trip_empty_and_separated_segments]` builds paths from `[]`, `[""]`, `["a/b"]` and `["a","b"]`. It asserts `decoded.segments() == parts`, so the accessor returns the original contents in order.
  - `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_paths_preserve_opaque_segments_and_separate_all_node_kinds]` asserts `path.segments() == expected` for many segment vectors, including opaque segments.
- **Ordered sequence.** `identities_remain_stable_and_fingerprinting_uses_the_supplied_snapshot` in `contracts.rs` asserts that `["a","b"]` differs from `["b","a"]`. It also asserts that `[]`, `[""]` and `["",""]` are mutually distinct, as are `["a"]` and `["a","a"]`, `["a/b"]` and `["a","b"]`, and the case, whitespace and Unicode variants. Segment boundaries, order and content therefore all matter for equality.
- **Private fields.** The `compile_fail` doctest on `struct[NodePath]` in `graph.rs` checks that `path.segments` is inaccessible. The struct carries a {test} marker, and `public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported inventory.
- **Trait implementations.**
  - `PartialEq` and `Eq`: asserted by the `assert_eq!` and `assert_ne!` calls above, and by the clone-equality check `*path == path.clone()`.
  - `Clone`: `path.clone()` is exercised in that same loop.
  - `Debug`: required by `assert_eq!` and `assert_ne!` on `NodePath` values, so it is checked at compile time.
  - `Hash`: `paths.insert(path.clone())` into a `HashSet` in the `sdk.rs` test. It is exercised for many distinct paths and for reconstructed-equal paths.
  - `Serialize` and `Deserialize`: the JSON round-trip test asserts that the decoded value equals the original, including for empty and separator-containing segments.

The tests assert the outcomes rather than just running the code, and all of them carry {test} references to the subject. I found no unacknowledged gap.
